# @sethlivingston/oneway-http

> A declarative TypeScript HTTP client for Node.js and browsers. Zero runtime dependencies.
> Every outcome — transport failures, decode failures, unmatched statuses — is a typed
> discriminated union. No exceptions for HTTP outcomes.

## Source

- Repo: https://github.com/sethlivingston/oneway-http
- npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@sethlivingston/oneway-http
- Spec: https://github.com/sethlivingston/oneway-http/blob/main/docs/SPEC.md

## Install

```bash
npm install @sethlivingston/oneway-http
# Optional: Zod for schema-validated JSON decoding
npm install zod
```

ESM only. No CommonJS build. Node.js ≥ 24.

## Core Concepts

### No exceptions for HTTP outcomes

`client.send()` always resolves — it never rejects for HTTP-level outcomes. Every outcome is a
`SendResult<R>`, a flat discriminated union on `.kind`.

### Declarative response maps

The caller declares up front which status codes to expect and how to decode each. Unmatched
statuses are returned explicitly, never silently swallowed.

### Affine requests

Each `Request` instance can only be sent once. Create a fresh one for each send (typically via a
factory function). Re-sending a consumed request returns `requestError.requestConsumed` — it does
not throw.

---

## Full API Reference

### createClient(spec)

```typescript
import { createClient } from "@sethlivingston/oneway-http";

const client = createClient({
  baseUrl: "https://api.example.com/",  // trailing slash optional — auto-normalized
  headers: { authorization: `Bearer ${token}` },
  query: { version: "2" },             // applied to every request
  responses: {                         // client-level defaults (request-level overrides)
    "4xx": Decode.json(ErrorSchema).as("apiError"),
    "5xx": Decode.discard().as("serverError"),
  },
  retry: true,                         // GET/HEAD, 3 attempts, 200ms–10s jitter backoff
  deadlineMs: 10_000,                  // whole-operation deadline (covers all retries)
  fetch: globalThis.fetch,             // injectable — use for testing or custom fetch
  diagnostics: { bodyPreviewBytes: 8192 },
});
```

`ClientSpec` fields:
- `baseUrl` — base URL. Automatically normalized to end with `/`.
- `headers` — default headers merged (case-insensitive) with each request's headers.
- `query` — default query params merged with each request's query params.
- `responses` — client-level `ResponseMap` layered under request-level map.
- `retry` — `true` | `false` | `RetryOptions`. Default: no retry.
- `deadlineMs` — positive integer. Covers all attempts + backoff + body reading.
- `fetch` — defaults to `globalThis.fetch`. Inject a mock for testing.
- `diagnostics.bodyPreviewBytes` — first N bytes captured for error diagnostics. Default: 8192.

### Request.create(spec)

```typescript
import { Request } from "@sethlivingston/oneway-http";

const req = Request.create({
  method: "POST",                              // "GET" | "POST" | "PUT" | "PATCH" | "DELETE" | "HEAD" | "OPTIONS" | "QUERY"
  path: ["v1", "users"],                       // joined as /v1/users and resolved against baseUrl
  // absoluteUrl: "https://other.com/webhook", // bypasses baseUrl entirely (use path OR absoluteUrl, not both)
  query: { page: "1" },
  headers: { "x-request-id": "abc" },
  body: Body.json({ name: "Alice" }),
  responses: {
    201: Decode.json(UserSchema).as("created"),
    409: Decode.json(ErrorSchema).as("conflict"),
  },
  retry: false,                                // override client policy for this request
  deadlineMs: 3000,                            // override client deadline for this request
});
```

`path` segments are individually `encodeURIComponent`-encoded. Numbers are stringified.
`absoluteUrl` bypasses `baseUrl` entirely — useful for webhooks, presigned URLs, external APIs.

### client.send(request, options?)

```typescript
const result = await client.send(req);
// or with an AbortSignal:
const result = await client.send(req, { signal: controller.signal });
```

Returns `Promise<SendResult<R>>`. Always resolves. Never rejects for HTTP-level outcomes.

### SendResult\<R\>

```typescript
type SendResult<R> =
  | { kind: "response";        response: R }
  | { kind: "transportError";  error: TransportError }
  | { kind: "decodeError";     status: number; headers: Headers; error: DecodeError; preview: BodyPreview }
  | { kind: "unhandledStatus"; status: number; headers: Headers; preview: BodyPreview }
  | { kind: "requestError";    error: RequestError };
```

- `response` — HTTP response received, matched a status in the `ResponseMap`, decoded successfully. `response.tag` is the string from `.as(tag)`. `response.body` is the decoded value.
- `transportError` — no HTTP response received. `error.kind`: `"aborted"` | `"timeout"` | `"network"`.
- `decodeError` — matched status, but body reading or schema validation failed.
- `unhandledStatus` — status not matched in the merged `ResponseMap`.
- `requestError` — request could not be formed. `error.kind`: `"bodySerializationFailed"` | `"requestConsumed"` | `"missingBaseUrl"` | `"duplicateResponseTag"` | `"invalidSpec"` | `"reservedResponseTag"`.

### Send.match(result, handlers)

Exhaustive dispatcher. TypeScript enforces all variants are handled.

```typescript
import { Send, type Matcher } from "@sethlivingston/oneway-http";

const value = Send.match(result, {
  created:    ({ body }) => body,           // body is typed as User
  conflict:   ({ body }) => null,           // body is typed as ErrorBody
  transportError:  (error)                           => { throw new Error(error.kind); },
  decodeError:     (error, status, headers, preview) => { throw new Error(error.kind); },
  unhandledStatus: (status, headers, preview)        => { throw new Error(`HTTP ${status}`); },
  requestError:    (error)                           => { throw new Error(error.kind); },
});
```

#### Reusable handler fragments

```typescript
import type { Matcher } from "@sethlivingston/oneway-http";

const sharedErrors: Partial<Matcher<typeof result, MyReturnType>> = {
  transportError:  (error)  => { throw new Error(error.kind); },
  decodeError:     (e, s)   => { throw new Error(`decode(${s}): ${e.kind}`); },
  unhandledStatus: (status) => { throw new Error(`HTTP ${status}`); },
  requestError:    (error)  => { throw new Error(error.kind); },
};

// Spread into each call site:
return Send.match(result, {
  ...sharedErrors,
  created: ({ body }) => body,
} satisfies Matcher<typeof result, MyReturnType>);
```

The `satisfies` keyword preserves per-handler return type inference. Use it on the final object.

### Body factories

```typescript
import { Body } from "@sethlivingston/oneway-http";

Body.none()                                           // no body
Body.json({ name: "Alice" })                          // application/json — serialized at send time
Body.text("hello")                                    // text/plain; charset=utf-8
Body.text("<p>hi</p>", "text/html")                   // custom Content-Type
Body.formUrlEncoded({ name: "Alice", role: "admin" }) // application/x-www-form-urlencoded
Body.bytes(new Uint8Array([0x89, 0x50]))               // raw bytes, no Content-Type
Body.bytes(data, "image/png")                         // raw bytes with Content-Type
```

`Body.json()` never throws — if `JSON.stringify` fails, `send()` returns `requestError.bodySerializationFailed`.

### Decode factories

```typescript
import { Decode } from "@sethlivingston/oneway-http";

Decode.none()                                   // strict: error if any body bytes present
Decode.discard()                                // safe: cancel body stream without reading
Decode.text()                                   // UTF-8 string; empty body → ""
Decode.json()                                   // JSON → unknown; empty body → decodeError.emptyBody
Decode.json(schema)                             // JSON → T (Zod schema validated)
Decode.bytes()                                  // Uint8Array
Decode.optional(Decode.json(schema))            // zero bytes → undefined; non-empty → T
```

Chain `.as(tag)` to create a `TaggedEntry` for use in a `ResponseMap`:

```typescript
Decode.json(UserSchema).as("user")      // TaggedEntry<User, "user">
Decode.discard().as("deleted")          // TaggedEntry<void, "deleted">
Decode.optional(Decode.text()).as("body") // TaggedEntry<string | undefined, "body">
```

### Response matching precedence

Specificity-first, then layer-first within each tier:

1. request exact status (e.g. `200`)
2. client exact status
3. request class matcher (e.g. `"2xx"`, `"4xx"`, `"5xx"`)
4. client class matcher
5. `unhandledStatus`

Exact always beats class regardless of which map it comes from.

### Retry policy

```typescript
// Default behavior when retry: true
// - methods: ["GET", "HEAD", "QUERY"]
// - maxAttempts: 3
// - retryableStatuses: [502, 503, 504]  (NOTE: 429 not included by default)
// - initialDelayMs: 200, maxDelayMs: 10_000

const client = createClient({
  retry: {
    methods: ["GET", "HEAD"],
    maxAttempts: 3,
    retryableStatuses: [429, 502, 503, 504],
    initialDelayMs: 200,
    maxDelayMs: 10_000,
  },
});

// Per-request: replaces the client policy entirely (not merged)
const req = Request.create({
  method: "POST",
  path: ["jobs"],
  retry: false,   // explicitly disable
  responses: { 202: Decode.json(JobSchema).as("accepted") },
});
```

---

## Common Patterns

### Basic GET with full handling

```typescript
import { createClient, Request, Decode, Send } from "@sethlivingston/oneway-http";
import { z } from "zod";

const UserSchema = z.object({ id: z.string(), name: z.string() });
const client = createClient({ baseUrl: "https://api.example.com/" });

async function getUser(id: string) {
  const req = Request.create({
    method: "GET",
    path: ["users", id],
    responses: {
      200: Decode.json(UserSchema).as("user"),
      404: Decode.discard().as("notFound"),
    },
  });

  return Send.match(await client.send(req), {
    user:            ({ body }) => body,
    notFound:        ()        => null,
    transportError:  (error)   => { throw new Error(error.kind); },
    decodeError:     (e, s)    => { throw new Error(`decode(${s}): ${e.kind}`); },
    unhandledStatus: (s)       => { throw new Error(`HTTP ${s}`); },
    requestError:    (error)   => { throw new Error(error.kind); },
  });
}
```

### Request factory pattern (reusable requests)

```typescript
// Define a factory function — each call returns a fresh Request (required: affine)
function getUser(id: string) {
  return Request.create({
    method: "GET",
    path: ["users", id],
    responses: { 200: Decode.json(UserSchema).as("user") },
  });
}

// Call site:
const result = await client.send(getUser("u-123"));
```

### Testing with an injected fetch

```typescript
const mockFetch: typeof globalThis.fetch = async () =>
  new Response(JSON.stringify({ id: "1", name: "Alice" }), {
    status: 200,
    headers: { "content-type": "application/json" },
  });

const client = createClient({
  baseUrl: "https://api.example.com/",
  fetch: mockFetch,
});
```

---

## Common Mistakes

### ❌ Forgetting `.as(tag)` on a decoder

```typescript
// WRONG — Decoder<T> is not a valid ResponseMap value
responses: { 200: Decode.json(UserSchema) }

// CORRECT
responses: { 200: Decode.json(UserSchema).as("user") }
```

TypeScript will catch this at compile time with a type error.

### ❌ Reusing a Request instance

```typescript
// WRONG — second send returns requestError.requestConsumed
const req = Request.create({ ... });
await client.send(req);
await client.send(req); // ← requestError.requestConsumed

// CORRECT — factory function produces a fresh Request each time
function myReq() { return Request.create({ ... }); }
await client.send(myReq());
await client.send(myReq());
```

### ❌ Using `path` without a `baseUrl`

```typescript
// WRONG — returns requestError.missingBaseUrl
const client = createClient({});  // no baseUrl
const req = Request.create({ method: "GET", path: ["users"], responses: {} });

// CORRECT — set baseUrl on the client, or use absoluteUrl on the request
const client = createClient({ baseUrl: "https://api.example.com/" });
// or:
Request.create({ method: "GET", absoluteUrl: "https://api.example.com/users", responses: {} });
```

### ❌ Expecting 429 retries with `retry: true`

The default `retryableStatuses` are `[502, 503, 504]`. 429 is not included:

```typescript
// Include 429 explicitly:
retry: { retryableStatuses: [429, 502, 503, 504] }
```

### ❌ Using `Decode.none()` where `Decode.discard()` is appropriate

```typescript
// Decode.none() — strict: returns decodeError.unexpectedBody if any bytes present
// Use for: HEAD responses, endpoints that guarantee no body (e.g., 204 No Content)
204: Decode.none().as("deleted")

// Decode.discard() — lenient: cancels body stream without reading
// Use for: responses where you don't care about the body (e.g., DELETE success)
200: Decode.discard().as("ok")
```

---

## Out of Scope (v1)

- Streaming request bodies
- Multipart form data (`multipart/form-data`)
- Credentials management / cookies
- Upload/download progress events
- Redirect control (`redirect` is always `"follow"`)
- CommonJS build
